title: God's Strength in Weakness
definition: God's strength in weakness is the truth that His grace is sufficient and His power is displayed through human limitation and dependence.
summary: God's grace is sufficient, and His power is made perfect in weakness.
christFocus: Jesus meets weak people with sustaining grace and displays His power through those who depend on Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Weakness is not meaningless to God. Scripture teaches that God's power is often displayed through human limitation, suffering, inability, and dependence.

Paul learned that God's grace was sufficient even when the thorn remained. Weakness became a place where the strength of Christ rested on him.

This doctrine does not romanticize pain, but it does reject the lie that weakness makes a person useless to God. Dependence may become the very place where God's strength is most clearly seen.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often feel ashamed of weakness and assume God only uses the strong. God's strength in weakness matters because it gives dignity, courage, and purpose to those who feel limited.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop pretending to be stronger than you are. Bring weakness to Christ, receive daily grace, and look for ways God can display His strength through dependence rather than self-sufficiency.
